parts.note: the article 'a' is the word for one
a bet is a gamble or wager

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hand placing a single wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so it is a verb for help.

clue.text: Paces about at home, close to staying, then getting away

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of paces are moved around into a new order

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from staying

explanation.surface: A restless person walks round the house before deciding to stay put, then leaves after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal, and 'close to' picks the final letter of 'staying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaping is fleeing or breaking free, a direct synonym for getting away.

indicators.note: eighty per cent of a five-letter word keeps its first four letters

parts.note: plush furnishings are luxurious and rich

explanation.surface: A description of opulence rated at better than eighty per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: The '+' sign that looks like part of the percentage is the definition: it is read as the word for that symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol + is spoken as the word meaning added to, as in two and two.

indicators.note: entering means the word for sin goes inside the other letters
flow suggests the letters of waste run loose and settle in a new order

parts.note: to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A rat's wrongdoing is to wander into a stream of sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flow' is the anagram signal for 'waste', and 'entering' puts the sin inside those rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown rat that lives in drains is commonly called by this name, a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Approach tailless urban feline from behind

indicators.note: reading from behind means the letters are taken from the back to the front
tailless means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: urban means of the city
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A street cat with no tail creeps up on someone from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urban' must be read as the noun city for 'tailless' to work; 'from behind' then turns the whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a method or line of attack chosen to achieve something, which is an approach.

clue.text: Accompanying dog into party about books

indicators.note: into here says the dog follows on directly from the party, the word fitted onto its end

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative party
a cur is a mongrel dog
re means about or concerning
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A dog wanders into a party and turns its attention to the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are concurrent happen at the same time, running alongside each other, so they are accompanying.

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the grid as coming down, a palindrome in a down light

parts.note: the setter reuses the definition word: looks means observes with the eyes, and that word reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Someone eyes another person from head to toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sees and looks are both verbs of using one's eyes, here in the third person singular.

clue.text: Herb Alpert's debut, one regularly covered by British Sign Language

indicators.note: covered by means these letters sit inside the abbreviation
regularly means the inserted letters are spaced evenly through the abbreviation, one between each pair

parts.note: BSL is the standard abbreviation for British Sign Language

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The trumpeter Herb Alpert's first appearance, interpreted for deaf viewers in sign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like Alpert's first name but is the definition. A and I go between the letters of BSL, one in each gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb much used in Italian cooking, an example of the category.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means intricate and detailed
to ..., as a verb, is to explain more fully

explanation.surface: A short remark that something is hard to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling is an adjective meaning intricate and a verb meaning to expand on or clarify something.

clue.text: Passing time with artist playing tennis

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword shorthand for an artist

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of tennis are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist whiles away the hours on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient lasts only a short while, so it is passing or fleeting.

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's joins the words as 'is'

explanation.surface: A convent schoolgirl is taught how to carry herself elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lesson' is a second definition: a class is also a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with class has elegance and stylish distinction, so the word is a synonym for style.

parts.note: the 's at the end of Leader's gives the letter S
a Kipper is a member of UKIP, the UK Independence Party, which campaigned to leave the EU

explanation.surface: A query whether a political leader backs a breakaway.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP is the UK Independence Party, a British party whose members are nicknamed Kippers. The S comes from the 's of 'Leader's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is a captain of a ship or team, the person in charge, so a leader.

clue.text: Power is rising by three quarters

indicators.note: in a down light rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: north, east and west are three of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Strength grows by seventy-five per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular strength or force, as in the sinews of war, so it is power.

clue.text: Anaesthetise small dog biting tot, else in trouble

indicators.note: biting means the dog's letters close around the others like jaws

parts.note: a pup is a young, small dog

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of tot and else are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A puppy nips a toddler and the household is thrown into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' puts UTTOSLEE, from 'in trouble' rearranging TOT ELSE, inside PUP after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone to sleep is to make them unconscious with drugs, which is to anaesthetise them.

clue.text: Wow! Not even posh journalist suffered an attack of the giggles

definitions.text: suffered an attack of the giggles

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

indicators.note: not even means the even-placed letters are dropped and the odd ones kept

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An awestruck reporter, oddly un-posh, collapses into helpless laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: To corpse is theatre slang for an actor breaking into laughter on stage. 'Not even' leaves P and S from 'posh'.
explanation.definitionFit: In acting, corpsing is spoiling a scene by laughing uncontrollably, which is an attack of the giggles.

definitions.meaning: in old London slang a wife is called 'my old duchess', shortened in a famous music-hall song
the nationality of people from the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Asking where an East End man's wife comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both London slang for a wife and the adjective for people of the Netherlands.

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard, not seen, so the clue goes by its sound

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A segment of a broadcast programme called After Dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time after dark, so the phrase works as a definition by description.

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned over, so the word for merely is turned round

parts.note: but can mean merely or only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A sluggish vessel that has simply turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is informal for a slow, clumsy boat.

clue.text: … their old money, trading capital for a billion workers

indicators.note: trading the capital for something means the first letter is swapped out for it

parts.note: following on from the clue about the Dutch, their old money was the guilder, used before the euro
B is an abbreviation for a billion

explanation.surface: The Dutch swapped their old currency, losing their capital for a vast sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back through the ellipsis to the Dutch of 16 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders are tradesmen who construct houses, a kind of workers.

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is dropped, here the front five letters

parts.note: overweight means too heavy

explanation.surface: Is the rowing team overweight? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which disguises its job of removing half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat crewed by eight oarsmen, so the word names a crew.

clue.text: Most of bottle satisfied special connoisseurs

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a gourd is a hollowed fruit used as a bottle
met means satisfied, as in met the demand

explanation.surface: Wine experts are pleased by most of a particular bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmets are experts in fine food and drink, a type of connoisseur.

clue.text: Dishes a world away, fine for the Springboks?

indicators.note: away suggests the letters of a world are sent off in a scattered order

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
the Springboks are the South African rugby team, so SA lads

explanation.surface: Fine meals far from home for the South African rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: A Waldorf salad of apple, celery and walnuts is a dish, so the plural is dishes.

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A query about the newest screen test in the film capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Latest is a superlative meaning newest or most up to date.

clue.text: Documents describe the end of government cuts

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the documents enclose a letter

parts.note: files are documents kept on record

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Official papers set out how a government will cut spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Documents' gives FILES, which wraps the T at the end of 'government'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fillets are boneless slices of meat or fish, cuts from the butcher.

indicators.note: keeps means the slow word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to inch is to creep slowly forward

indicators.note: dashing suggests the letters of out rush about into a new order

explanation.surface: A slowcoach is unable to hurry outside, yet stays modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creep' is a verb here, not a person; 'dashing' signals the anagram and 'keeps' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well informed about current events is being up-to-date.

definitions.meaning: a place to lodge for the night
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word after Golf for G is the one for H

explanation.surface: Choosing lodgings after a round on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place to stay, and the same word is the radio code for H, following G.

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
air is a mixture of gases

explanation.surface: A jolt from a burst of hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mass of it, so the word works through that idiom.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty and the article 'a' gives one

indicators.note: sexy suggests the letters of maidens get excited and rearranged

explanation.surface: A womaniser who has worked his way through fifty-one alluring young women.
explanation.definitionFit: A man known for charming and seducing women is described by this phrase.

indicators.note: through means the letters run inside the given word

explanation.surface: A sprint across the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair and spirit, the same as élan, panache.

clue.text: King managed to go up and annoy

indicators.note: in a down light to go up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A monarch arranged a rise in order to irritate people.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark is British informal for irritate or annoy.

clue.text: One should look thoroughly for trendy magazine wanting adult's clothing

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letters named are taken out

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine

indicators.note: clothing is what is on the outside, so the outer letters of adult are taken

explanation.surface: A fashionable magazine that has lost its grown-up's outfit should be examined closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly. 'clothing' means the outside letters of 'adult', and 'wanting' takes them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is someone whose job is to examine things carefully.

clue.text: Change shirt owned by real model

indicators.note: owned by means the shirt is held within the other letters
model suggests the letters of real are shaped anew

parts.note: T is short for T-shirt

explanation.surface: A genuine model swaps a shirt from their own wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' turns REAL into ALER, and 'owned by' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change or modify it.
